title: Lancaster Street ramp closure deferred for Kitchener input
subtitle: Cambridge transit expansion, Ayr waste collection, landfill expropriation, ION winter reliability, Charles Street terminal and growth estimates
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended deferring a decision on closing the Lancaster Street and Highway 85 ramps {{vote:m2}}. Staff said the ramps have a high collision rate and low use, and that closing them would allow a key north-south cycling link. Several members wanted Kitchener's council to be better informed first. Staff warned that a delay could cost the Region its window to coordinate with the Ministry of Transportation. The matter is to return by April 4, and possibly to Council on March 22.

The committee also recommended Grand River Transit service improvements for Cambridge, starting September 4, 2023 {{vote:m11}}. It recommended extending waste and recycling collection to Swan Street in downtown Ayr at no added cost to the 2023 operating budget {{vote:m12}}. Through the consent agenda it recommended expropriating a Wilmot property for landfill soil management {{vote:m9}}, among other items {{vote:m3}}.

The committee received reports on Indigenous space needs, the Charles Street terminal site, regional population estimates and ION winter operations. A closed session followed the meeting. The minutes do not report any decisions from it.

decisions.item: Lancaster Street and Highway 85 ramp closure
decisions.detail: The committee recommended deferring the ramp closure decision to no later than the April 4, 2023 committee cycle, and possibly to Council on March 22, 2023 {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended approving transit service improvements for the Cambridge service area, effective September 4, 2023.
The committee recommended extending the waste and recycling collection area to Swan Street, from Stanley Street to Fowler Street, with no increase to the 2023 operating budget.
The committee recommended approving expropriation of the Wilmot property for soil management needs for the remaining life of the Waterloo landfill.

decisions.item: Cedar Creek and Trussler roundabout expropriation
decisions.detail: The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to start expropriation of lands and temporary easements for a roundabout at Cedar Creek Road, Trussler Road and County Road 8.
The committee recommended approving the design concept for University Avenue from Albert Street to Weber Street, filing a Notice of Completion, and adding reserved bike lanes.
The committee recommended endorsing the 11 municipal drinking water licences and their operational plans, and received the 2022 drinking water reports for information.

debate: A delegate opposed closing the Lancaster ramps. The delegate said closing them would add traffic to the Bridgeport ramps, where turning east is already difficult. The delegate also questioned spending on removing existing infrastructure and said bike lanes could coexist with traffic.

Staff said the ramps have about four times the expected collisions because of a weaving pattern, and far less traffic than nearby ramps. Staff also said closure would enable a protected north-south cycling connection and that the Ministry of Transportation would fund the work.
One councillor asked why a rare, significant change reached the Kitchener area council so late. Staff said Kitchener staff had earlier indicated a council report was not required.

Councillors split on deferral. Some worried about missing the Ministry of Transportation's design window, which could mean separate work and two closures. Others said a short delay was a reasonable courtesy and that Council could change the recommendation on March 22.

On ION winter operations, the operator described freezing rain as ice that builds up on the overhead wire. It said it is adding scrapers, de-icing fluid and consolidated service. One councillor asked why a global operator was still learning. Others urged keeping the disruptions in perspective.
